newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rival telecom bidders meet Singapore regulators.
newsitem.headline: Rival telecom bidders meet Singapore regulators.

text.p: Bidders for licenses to enter Singapore's telephone services market said on Friday a meeting with industry regulators on future competition policy had shed light on the issue but more details were needed.
"I wouldn't say I was happier. Things are a little clearer now, but there is still more to talk about," said one consortium executive, who declined to be identified.

"There was plenty of detail. TAS (Telecommunication Authority of Singapore) had obviously worked hard for this meeting," added the executive, speaking to Reuters after two hours of discussions on Friday.
The meeting was called after TAS announced earlier this month it would invite bids for further commercial phone services licenses to begin operation from 2002.

The three consortiums tendering for an expected two licenses to provide basic phone services from 2000 were caught off-guard by the news and complained that the extra competition could destroy business plans which had formed the basis of their bids.
Telecoms analysts say it takes about five years of competition-free operation for telephone companies to start to make decent profits.
One consortium groups a unit of the state-run Singapore Technologies group, Singapore Power, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and British Telecommunications Plc under the StarHub banner.
TelecomOne groups Singapore Press Holdings Ltd, Keppel Telecom, Cable & Wireless plc and Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd .
The third consortium links SembCorp, Singapore Mass Rapid Transit and Worldcom Inc.
TAS declined to comment immediately on the outcome of the meeting but a spokeswoman said a statement would be issued later on Friday.
